intro.text: Hi! Welcome in. I'll be your guide for this little tour. Quick confession: I'm an AI voice. I was made on Mike's Mac Studio, down in his basement, same as everything else on this website. Mike spent thirteen years keeping a carrier network running, and he really doesn't like doing anything twice. Scroll at your own pace. I'll keep up.

tldr.text: Okay, the short version, for the busy ones. Thirteen years as a network engineer at Charter. Python automation since 2020. Then two years on a dev-ops team. And now? AI tools, built and run on his own hardware. That's it. Short and sweet.

thesis.text: Mike lives by one rule, and honestly, it's a good one. Do it once, by hand. Do it twice, and grumble about it. The third time? A computer does it. The tools keep changing. The rule doesn't.

story.text: So here's how he got here. Tech school. Then Charter, in 2013, turning up fiber circuits by the thousand. A spreadsheet that turned an hour of work into five minutes. Then Python. Then a dev-ops team. And in June of 2026, one very big week: a new baby on Tuesday, and a closed office on Friday. Talk about a plot twist.

numbers.text: So what did all those scripts actually add up to? Thousands of routers and other network devices, kept on standard, week after week. Hundreds of thousands of devices, found, inventoried and kept secure. And the hours nobody had to spend doing it all by hand? Honestly, too many to count.

lab.text: And now, the workshop beneath the house. Watch your head. A control room for all his AI. A stock dashboard that pinned people's tweets right onto the price chart. A house voice named Thaddeus, who reads tornado warnings at three in the morning. Monitoring that makes failures loud. And a garden planner called GrowYear, which is live on the internet now. His family uses most of it. Some of them even like it.

before.text: None of this started with AI. Long before any of it, Mike was wiring up garage doors, plant waterers, and pepper sensors, by hand. Tinkerers are a stubborn bunch. The AI just made him faster.

garden.text: A gardener who starts young gets about sixty gardens in a lifetime. Sixty. That's not very many, is it? That's why Mike builds these tools: so the computers take more of the chores, and his family gets more of him.

built.text: Okay, this part is fun. Everything you see and hear on this page was made by AI models running on Mike's Mac Studio. The pictures, the music, and, yes, me. And the page itself? It comes to you from a Raspberry Pi in his basement, through a tunnel, by way of a satellite. Pretty cool, right?

how.text: How he works. Do it twice, then script it. Be the first one in. Make failures loud. And let the AI ask before it does anything that matters. Good rules, if you ask me.

next.text: So, what's he looking for? A small team that wants the boring stuff gone. Anywhere from Madison to Milwaukee, hybrid if he can get it. If that sounds like your team, you're in the right place.

contact.text: And that's the tour! If any of this sounds like your team, his email is right there. Go on, write to him. Okay, cool. Thanks for stopping by!
